title: Dance halls and street battles of bands
summary: He names the public halls where bands played. Bands advertised dances from trucks and when they met in the street they battled, the last band standing winning.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Dance halls, lake resorts and where bands played

blocks.x: Well, do you remember what places they played at the time? Yeah.

Different halls, like the Franz Ammi, that's at North Robinson and St. Anthony Street. The Economy Hall on the Eastern Line between Villery and Murray. And the Cooperators Hall, known as the Hopes Hall. That's on North Liberty between St. Fort and Dumaine Street. Then there's the Poiseuilins Hall down on Villery near Ennett Street. Then there's the New Hall.
Those were mostly for private dances?

No, public dances. They'd hire the hall and give advertisement for it. They wouldn't give a ball unless they'd have advertisement. No truck. Many as three and four bands would be out on the street on one Sunday. Whenever they'd meet up together, that was a battle of music. What did they do? Try and play each other down for loudness? No, for everything. Sometimes it'd stop the traffic. And the band that would stay there the longest would be considered the winner.
